text.p: Here are highlights of stories reported by Hungary's press, based on information by Nepszabadsag's Hungary Around the Clock service. For further details on how to subscribe to Hungary Around the Clock, please contact Monica Kovacs at (361) 351 2440 or fax your request to (361) 351 7141.
ALL PAPERS
- An unidentified person shot and killed an entrepreneur in Budapest Wednesday evening.
- In his letter to Romanian counterpart Victor Ciorbea, Prime Minister Gyula Horn said he is pressing for a prime ministerial meeting at the earliest possible date.
- The Democratic Federation of Hungarians in Romania has received eight state secretary posts in the Romanian cabinet, according to a coalition agreement worked out late Tuesday.
- A stable 2-3 percent GDP growth will probably begin next year, said Industry and Trade Minister Szabolcs Fazekas.

- Transport Minister Karoly Lotz signed a concession agreement with Compagnia General Costruzioni of Italy yesterday, under which the firm will build out and operate electrical lines above Hungarian railway routes.
- Dutch bank ABN Amro will raise Magyar Hitel Bank's capital by $137 million, well over the $100 million reported earlier, according to the sale contract signed yesterday.
- Welfare Minister Mihaly Kokeny announced Wednesday that the sum of family allowance will grow next year depending on the number of children.
- The Defence Ministry budget will increase by 23 percent, from HUF 79 billion to HUF 97 billion next year, announced Defence Minister Gyorgy Keleti.
- The Hungarian technical contingent comprising 143 professional officers arrived in Okucani, Croatia on Wednesday to take part in the work of the Bosnian Stabilisation Force.
- The US-based human rights organisation Freedom House lists Hungary as a free country in its annual report.
- BNP-Dresdner Bank purchased about 90 percent of Arany Broker yesterday.
MAGYAR HIRLAP
- The government is likely to pass a decree spelling out the details of the amendment to the act on public finances at its weekly meeting today.
- The State Privatisation and Holding Co. plans to sell the truck manufacturer Raba to financial and strategic investors.
- Private savings went up by HUF 55.7 billion in November.
- Sluggish demand and increasing interest rates marked this week's auctions of discount treasury bills on Tuesday and Wednesday.
VILAGGAZDASAG
- The Hungarian economy has been judged to be "largely free" by the Washington-based Heritage Foundation. The country is on the 64th on the world list.
- Ringa Rt., a manufacturer of meat products, has boosted its revenues by 77 percent in the past two years, while exports went up by 120 percent, managing director Ferenc Janko said.
NEPSZABADSAG
- The sale of the national electricity company MVM is the most important privatisation deal still ahead, said Privatisation Minister Judit Csiha.

- Industry and Trade Minister Szabolcs Fazekas said that the Belgian investor Tractabel, which had threatened to withdraw its investment in the power plant Dunamenti Eromu due to lower energy prices, recently reached an energy price agreement with MVM.
NAPI GAZDASAG
- Compensation coupons worth some HUF 100 billion at face value have been withdrawn from the market so far, said State Privatisation and Holding Co. managing director.
